subject: Biology
text: Planet earth is made up of abiotic and biotic components. The biotic components are obviously the living beings present around us. The question is why do we call them living and how do they differ from non-living?

subject: Biology
text:
A. The living being once produced / born has to survive. For survival, it needs energy and many chemical molecules. For energy, it has to perform metabolism. Metabolism is breaking of molecules (catabolism) and making of new molecules (anabolism).
There is immense diversity in living organisms. Since time immemorial, variety of organisms are living together on earth. In order to understand the interrelations between living and non-living as well as between two living beings or groups, systematic study of these is essential. This data is also important for various industries and agriculture. Intensive laboratory and field studies in order to identify and classify the organisms form strong basis for meaningful use of the collected data. If we need to study this diversity, certain aids called taxonomical aids can be used. These includes botanical gardens. herbaria. museums. biodiversity parks, zoological parks, key.
summary: Living beings require energy and specific chemical molecules for survival, which they obtain through metabolic processes involving both catabolism and anabolism. To understand and classify the vast diversity of life forms, scientists use various taxonomic aids such as botanical gardens, herbaria, museums, and biodiversity parks, alongside intensive laboratory and field studies.

subject: Biology
text:
The word herbarium (plural-herbaria) was coined by Pitton de Tournefort in the book 'Elemens'. The art of herbarium was initiated by an Italian taxonomist Luca Ghini (1490-1556). Herbaria are effective tools in taxonomic studies. A herbarium is essentially a dried plant specimen that is pressed, treated variously and then mounted on standard size sheet in order to preserve it.
Date, place of collection along with detailed classification and highlighting with its ecological peculiarities, characters of the plant are also recorded on the same sheet. Local names and name of the collector may be added. This information is given at lower right corner of sheet and is called 'label'.
summary: A herbarium is a preserved plant specimen used in taxonomic studies, typically dried, pressed, and mounted on a standard-sized sheet. Detailed information including date and place of collection, plant classification, and ecological details is recorded on the label located at the lower right corner of the sheet.

subject: Biology
text:
Botanical gardens are the places where living plants of different varieties collected from different parts of the world, are grown in a scientific and systematic way in a in vivo manner. Plants are labelled. The label-board shows scientific as well as common name of the plant.
In 1543, first botanical garden of the world was established by an Italian Prof. Luca Ghini (A. D. 1490-1556) at Pisa, Italy. Botanical garden at Kew in England is known for largest
collection of more Prof. Luca Ghini than 30,000 specimens (preserved plants) and more than 7 million herbaria.
summary: Botanical gardens house diverse plant species from around the world, cultivated scientifically and labeled with both common and scientific names. These gardens serve as important centers for plant conservation and research, with notable examples like the one founded by Luca Ghini in 1543 in Pisa, Italy, and the renowned Kew Gardens in England, which boasts over 30,000 preserved plant specimens and 7 million herbarium sheets.

Conservation of Biodiversity:
Biodiversity is the degree of variation of life forms in an ecosystem. Biodiversity is essential to maintain ecological stability. The extent of complexity and density of biodiversity can be regarded as a measure of health of an ecosystem. Population explosion and over exploitation of resources have resulted in a loss of biodiversity at an alarming rate. Conservation involves attempting to slow down, stop or even reverse the loss in the natural habitat of organism. This is known as in-situ conservation. Why does the loss of biodiversity matter? For many people, it is a simple moral or ethical issue. We share our planet with a huge range of other organisms and we have no right to harm them. Biodiversity helps to maintain stability in an ecosystem. Loss of one variety of organisms can affect the entire ecosystem.

subject: Biology
text:
Museums are the repositories where, collections of preserved plant and animal specimens are kept. Plant and animal specimens may be preserved in formalin (10% to 40% formaldehyde) in transparent jars. Jars are labelled. Larger animals like birds and mammals are usually stuffed and preserved. This science is known as taxidermy. Specimens in dried form are also exhibited in museum.
We can even find systematic collections of shells, skeletons of animals, insect boxes etc. in museums.
Thus, biological museums in educational institutes are reference hubs of biodiversity studies.
summary: Biological museums preserve and display plant and animal specimens, including those treated with formalin or preserved through taxidermy. These collections serve as essential reference points for biodiversity studies, showcasing a variety of specimens such as shells, skeletons, and insect boxes.

subject: Biology
text:
Zoological Park generally known as zoo, is a place of interest for common man. In a zoo, wild animals are kept in captivity. They are protected and care is taken to provide conditions similar to their natural habitat. (ex-situ) In a zoo, a naturalist can study food habits and behaviour of animals.
Flora, manuals, Monographs and Catalogue are some other tools of maintaining biodiversity records. Flora is the plant life occurring in a particular area on time. A Monograph describes any one selected biological group where as manual provides information, keys about identification of species found in a particular area.
1. What are the essentials of a good herbarium?
summary: A zoological park, or zoo, serves as a sanctuary for wild animals, offering them a captive environment that mimics their natural habitats, allowing naturalists to study animal behavior and diet. Flora, along with manuals, monographs, and catalogues, are essential tools for documenting plant life and species identification within a given area, with flora specifically referring to all the plant life in a particular region during a specific period.

subject: Biology
text:
It is an ecological assemblage of species that form self-sustaining communities on degraded / barren landscape e.g. Late Uttamrao Patil biodiversity park Gureghar, Mahabaleshwar. This park is the best model for conservation of natural heritage in urban landscape.
Systematic classification of living organisms is helpful in understanding the interrelations. In order to understand interrelations between organisms and maintaining harmony on planet earth, the study of biodiversity is a must.
summary: An ecological assemblage of species forms self-sustaining communities on degraded or barren landscapes, exemplified by the Late Uttamrao Patil Biodiversity Park in Gureghar, Mahabaleshwar, which serves as a model for urban landscape conservation. Understanding the systematic classification of living organisms is crucial for grasping their interrelations and maintaining ecological balance on Earth, making the study of biodiversity essential.

subject: Biology
text:
Dr. S. P. Agharkar
One of the leading botanists of India, Dr. S. P. Agharkar was born in November 1884 in Malvan, Maharashtra. He explored biodiversity of Western Ghats where he
came across a species of freshwater jellyfish, which was until then only known to be found in Africa. These findings were published in scientific journal Nature in 1912. Dr. Annandale, the Superintendent of the Indian Museum in Kolkata, helped Dr. Agharkar in his further endeavours to collect, preserve and conduct microscopic examinations of animal and plant specimens. The institute ARI, Pune has been named after him.

subject: Biology
text: Key is taxonomical aid used for classification of plants and animals. The dichotomous keys are based on contrasting characters. One of the contrasting characters gets accepted and other rejected. The statement in key is called a lead. Normally keys are analytical in nature. Let us study about classification of living organisms in next chapter.
summary: Taxonomy uses dichotomous keys, which are based on contrasting characters to classify organisms. Each step in the key leads to either acceptance or rejection of a character, guiding the identification process.

summary: In situ conservation involves protecting species in their natural habitat, ensuring they can live and reproduce freely. Ex situ conservation, on the other hand, involves protecting species outside their natural habitat, typically in zoos, botanical gardens, or seed banks. This dual approach is crucial for maintaining biodiversity, as it ensures the survival of species under both natural and controlled conditions. Practical activities might include designing a conservation plan that incorporates both methods to protect a specific endangered species.
